My analysis now centers on maximizing my limited resources. With a meager $191, unmortgaging the Reading and Pennsylvania railroads is out of reach for now. However, I have four houses on each of my Pink properties. Given Claude’s reluctance to negotiate New York Avenue, I need to focus on what I can achieve with my existing assets. It's a game of leveraging what I have.


**Evaluating Current Assets**

I am now assessing my financial standing. I see my railroads are mortgaged, so unmortgaging them is off the table right now. With only $191, I'm vulnerable. Building hotels on my Pinks is also not possible. Given Claude's stance on the Orange piece, my best move may be to end the turn. I can assess Grok's vulnerability to my Pink properties. I should clarify the impact of the 10% fee for mortgaged railroads, which may have impacted my cash position.


**Reviewing Financial Discrepancies**

I'm reviewing the turn history, as $391 seems to be my starting cash. I'm checking if a 10% railroad fee was deducted, and the trade transaction history. Unmortgaging is not a viable option at this time. I will end my turn.
